In general, you can't just play around with single molecules unless you get them down to near absolute zero. Molecules are constantly trying to rip themselves apart and any time the internal energy of the molecule is below kT (Boltzmann*Temp) it'll spontaneously break up. The molecule in question has to be scaled against kT.

Even if you want to "print" a stable final molecule, the transitional species still have an activation energy that must be overcome. This is the limiting factor in most reactions -- even if the product is more stable than the reactants, its not spontaneous if you can't overcome the activation energy.

Basically, a bunch of criteria have to occur for a reaction to flow from reactants to products -- the product has to have a higher Gibbs free energy than the reactants, enough energy has to be added to system to reach overcome activation, the product must be stable at whatever ambient temperature is chosen, etc.

Being able to print molecules would require building of the molecule from atoms through reactions. Organic chemists can already "build" pretty amazing things, such as nanoputians (pictures of humans built out of atoms) and nanocars (car made out of molecules) that actually have rolling wheels.
